docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This site stores links to GLD.SerializerBenchmark and to the Mojo gld-* libraries.

The gld-* libraries target Mojo 1.1.

Serialization turns an in-memory value into an ordered sequence of bytes. Deserialization rebuilds a value from those bytes. Programs do this when a value has to be stored or sent.

Serialization 101 on the benchmark explains this idea from three perspectives:

  • Historical perspective
  • Data science perspective
  • Engineering perspective

docs.title: Mojo serializers
docs.text:
These libraries target Mojo 1.1. They were written so a Mojo program can encode and decode these standards. The runtime and the code generator are written in Mojo. They do not wrap, link, or vendor a C, C++, or Rust library.

Schema-less means a decoder can walk a value without a schema. Schema means a decoder needs a schema.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
A serialization standard is the published specification for a format. A reader and a writer follow that specification so they agree on the bytes.

The full list of standards is on the benchmark's Compliance page.

The Mojo libraries on this site cover the standards below:

  • JSON
  • YAML
  • TOML
  • CBOR
  • MessagePack
  • BSON
  • Amazon Ion
  • Smile
  • Protocol Buffers
  • Apache Avro
  • FlatBuffers

The benchmark groups serializers into families, including schema-driven formats and schema-less formats. That grouping is explained on Serialization categories.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Schema means a decoder needs a schema. Schema-less means a decoder can walk a value without one.
